title: Kizzy Kalu: Filipino nurses lured with H-1B “nurse instructor” jobs, forced to work in Colorado nursing homes
summary: Through his company Foreign Healthcare Professionals Group, Kizzy Kalu of Highlands Ranch, Colorado, recruited nurses, mainly from the Philippines, charging fees of typically $6,500 for H-1B visas on 41 petitions that claimed they would work as nurse instructors at Adam University for $72,000 a year; the university was defunct. On arrival the nurses were placed as ordinary nurses in Colorado long-term-care facilities at about $20 an hour, Kalu kept roughly 40% of their earnings, demanded $800 to $1,200 a month, and threatened visa cancellation, deportation and a $25,000 contract penalty. A federal jury in Denver convicted him in July 2013 on 89 counts including forced labour, trafficking, visa fraud and money laundering; in February 2014 he was sentenced to 130 months in prison and ordered to pay $3,790,338.55 in restitution to about 26 nurses. A co-defendant received probation. The Tenth Circuit affirmed in June 2015.
